features: WHAT THE FORM ACTUALLY ASKED FOR — In the previous release we wrote that the printable F24 form could not be produced yet, because it needed fields postponed to 1.11: signatory, role code, intermediary, direct-debit IBAN. Then we opened the form published by the Italian Revenue Agency and went through it box by box: those fields are not on the sheet. They belong to the electronic filing format and to tax returns. Everything the form really asks for was already in place, and from this release the model can be printed.
NO DATABASE CHANGES: no migrations, no new columns, no data touched. The printout reads what was already there.
THREE COPIES, LIKE THE REAL FORM: two for the bank or post office, one for whoever makes the payment. The direct-debit authorisation appears only on the first copy, the one that stays at the counter.

Only the Treasury section is filled in. Social security, Regions, property tax and other bodies stay empty and present, exactly as on the pre-printed form: removing them would give a cleaner sheet and a different model from the one the recipient expects to receive. «Office code» and «assessment code» also stay blank, since the official guidance reserves them for amounts due following a tax assessment. TOTAL B stays empty rather than zero: with no credit offsetting there is nothing to declare in that column, and a «0.00» written there would report an offset of zero euros that does not exist.

AMOUNTS FOLLOW THE AGENCY'S RULES, which are three and all differ from how an amount is written on screen: always two decimal digits even when they are zeros, no thousands separator inside the euro boxes, and never a minus sign — the direction is already carried by the two columns, debit and credit. So «€ 1,060.00» becomes «1060» and «00» in two separate boxes.

The file gets a name you can find again, built on the due date, for example F24-scad-2026-06-16-12.pdf. The trailing number is the payment slip's id, and it is needed because two slips can legitimately share a due date: the two thresholds mature together on 16 December, and a slip with more than six rows is split into two forms for the same date. Without that number, downloading both would overwrite the first.

A reversed or cancelled payment slip prints with a watermark. It stays viewable and reprintable, because it must be kept for ten years, but printed without warning it would be indistinguishable from a live one — and paying it twice is a mistake the software can prevent on its own.

If the fiscal address is missing from the building's details the printout still works, and those boxes come out empty to be completed by hand. The payment slip page says so beforehand, which is the last moment the information is still useful: at the counter it is too late. It is not a block — whether a document is ready is the administrator's call.

WORTH KNOWING: PAPER IS NOT FOR EVERYONE. The Agency's guidance requires electronic filing for VAT-registered taxpayers and for anyone offsetting credits; an ordinary building association is neither, and can go to the counter. The sheet is also a facsimile: it reproduces the sections, order and field names of the official form but not its logo, and acceptance remains up to the counter.

The transcription sheet is not retired: they are two documents for two different actions. The transcription sheet lists the fields in the order you type them into online banking, the model is the sheet you hand over. Both are now available on the payment slip page and in the schedule menu.

Under the hood: converting amounts for the form is a separate function rather than a parameter of the one that formats for the screen, because the Agency's rules contradict Italian formatting on two points out of three. The total on the model is summed from the rows instead of read from the header, since on the sheet TOTAL A is by definition the sum of the column above it. The six Treasury rows printed on the sheet and the point at which a payment slip is split in two are the same number in two different places, and there is now a test keeping them tied together: if they diverged, a seven-row slip would lose the seventh without telling anyone. Twenty new tests cover the model's layout data and the amount formatting rules.
